posts.author: Hemanpower
posts.text: In fact, Groww was recently added to the FTSE All-World Index and MSCI index. When a stock joins FTSE All-World or MSCI, every fund that tracks that index — ETFs, index mutual funds, pension funds mandated to mirror the benchmark — has to buy the stock, regardless of what they think. This puts the stock on the radar of large international institutional investors who often restrict themselves to index constituents, or who use the index as their starting universe for research.

posts.author: Hemanpower
posts.text: Dear @sangi , This isn’t new , Groww has seen repeated block deals recently, including 7.78 crore shares worth nearly ₹1,500 crore in two trades just before this. This is typical post-IPO lock-in expiry pattern and not a signal of company weakness: Groww listed in Nov 2025, and early venture investors (Ribbit Capital, and previously Peak XV Partners/Sequoia in a separate May 2026 deal) are using block deals to gradually monetize their pre-IPO stakes now that lock-in restrictions have lifted.

posts.author: Aiyappaa
posts.text: I closely follow the broking industry. Groww gets around two-thirds of its brokerage revenue from options trading. Two developments are currently taking place. The first is a broking app called Sahi , which has started attracting options buyers with its gamified mobile options-trading experience, similar to video-game controls. Sahi currently charges ₹8 per order, while Groww charges ₹20. In fact, both Sahi and Dhan are reportedly adding new clients from Zerodha and Groww.
